explanation: Track a deficit for each keyword: one minus its count in the active window. Adding a word reduces the number of missing keywords only when its deficit crosses zero. Once every deficit is nonpositive, shrink from the left while recording better intervals.
timeComplexity: O(n + k) expected time. Each window endpoint advances at most n times after O(k) initialization. The entry-count bound treats word hashing/comparison as constant; include examined character lengths when words are unbounded.
spaceComplexity: O(k) auxiliary space for keyword counts. At most k keyword counts are stored.

correctness: Each deficit equals required count minus current window count, and remaining counts unsatisfied requirements. When remaining is zero, the window covers all keywords. Advancing left explores every shorter suffix until a required word becomes absent. At the right endpoint of an optimal interval this process considers an interval no longer than it, proving minimality.
walkthrough: For [oak, cedar, ash, oak, elm, ash] and keywords {oak, ash, elm}, the window first covers everything at indices [0, 4]. Removing oak at 0 preserves another oak at 3; removing cedar at 1 loses no keyword. This reaches [2, 4], containing ash, oak, elm in three entries. Return (2, 4); the protocol checks length 3. The callable returns inclusive zero-based endpoints. The executable walkthrough expected value is their length after the wrapper validates keyword coverage.
edgeCases: Duplicate occurrences in the paragraph must not count as distinct keywords.
Irrelevant words at either edge can be removed.
The input set determines keyword membership; a covering interval is guaranteed by this exercise.
